clue.text: Go mad, like parts of France?

parts.note: to go is to depart, leave
mental is slang for mad, crazy

explanation.surface: An invitation to run wild in the style of the French regions.
explanation.walkthrough: France is divided into administrative areas called départements, so something relating to them is, playfully, of a department.
explanation.definitionFit: France's regions are called départements, so belonging to them is an adjective from that word.

clue.text: Popular protest movement out of control

parts.note: a demo is a short form of demonstration, a protest march
a tic is an involuntary twitch, a movement one cannot control

explanation.surface: A mass protest march that has got out of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Demotic means of the common people, in ordinary popular use.

clue.text: Mountain route taken by. English and French over the hill

parts.note: a route through mountains

explanation.surface: English and French travellers crossing a hill by a mountain track.
explanation.walkthrough: The print has a stray full stop after 'by'. 'Taken by' just joins the pieces; the word borrowed from French means past its best.
explanation.definitionFit: Passé is a borrowing from French meaning out of date, past one's prime.

clue.text: The back row score again

parts.note: the rear is the back of something
a range is a row or line, as of mountains or houses

explanation.surface: Seats in the back row of a stadium, perhaps, and a second goal.
explanation.definitionFit: To score music again is to make a new arrangement of it, setting it out afresh.

clue.text: Principal moving between German banks

explanation.surface: A chief figure shuttling from one German bank to another.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'banks' are riverbanks, not financial houses: the Main is a river flowing through Frankfurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Main means chief or leading; the Main is also a German river flowing between its banks.

clue.text: To shoot up a politician is futile

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for shooting is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to gun is to shoot
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: Shooting a politician would achieve nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GUN into NUG, as the answer runs down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory means of no value or effect, worthless.

clue.text: Investor Disraeli sided with

explanation.surface: A financial backer whose side the Victorian prime minister took.
explanation.walkthrough: Disraeli, in an 1864 speech on evolution, declared himself 'on the side of the angels'. A theatrical backer is also called by this word.
explanation.definitionFit: A backer of a theatre production is a financier; Disraeli famously aligned himself with heavenly beings.

clue.text: Unhappy term exemplified in public school?

explanation.surface: A bad term at a famous fee-paying school.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'public school' is an exclusive private fee-paying school, so the name is a wrong label. 'Term' also tempts as a school term.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong or inappropriate name is an ill-chosen label; Britain's private schools are oddly called public.

clue.text: Win back queen when last piece is moved up

indicators.note: in a down clue moving a letter up takes it earlier in the word

parts.note: Regina is Latin for queen, as in the royal cipher
the final letter of the Latin word for queen

explanation.surface: Recovering a chess queen once the last piece has been advanced.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture misleads: the final A of REGINA climbs two places to sit before the I.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain is to recover or get something back.

clue.text: Film a ruler getting things confused

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on glass
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A movie in which a monarch muddles everything up.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistaking is misunderstanding, taking one thing for another.

clue.text: Chaps heard making appearance outside

indicators.note: heard signals that the word for chaps is spoken rather than written

parts.note: guys are chaps, men

explanation.surface: Men overheard making an entrance out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward appearance or semblance, often a false one.

clue.text: Right-minded person he included in speculation

indicators.note: included signals that he goes inside the word for a right-winger

parts.note: a Tory is a conservative, on the political right

explanation.surface: A conservative thinker adding his guesswork to the discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right-minded' means politically right-wing here, not virtuous.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a speculative explanation, a conjecture.

clue.text: Female sprinter second in race in state capital

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the name of the city

parts.note: Atlanta is the capital of the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: second in picks the second letter of the word race

explanation.surface: A woman runner comes second in a race held in a US state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Atalanta, of Greek myth, was a huntress who outran all suitors except one who dropped golden apples.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Atalanta was a fleet-footed huntress who raced her suitors.

clue.text: In centre of Monaco, is taken round this building?

indicators.note: taken round means the combination is turned back to front
In puts the word is inside the middle letters
centre of takes the letters of Monaco without its first and last

explanation.surface: A tour of a famous building in the heart of Monte Carlo.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a description of the Monte Carlo building; 'taken round' turns the combined letters back to front, so the word is read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Monte Carlo's best-known building is its gambling house, so the clue points to that place.

clue.text: It could result in a fine piece of writing

definitions.text: It could result in a fine

explanation.surface: A well-written passage that might earn a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's penalty, which may be a fine, is a court's ruling; a grammatical unit of writing has the same name.

clue.text: Students producing original pieces

parts.note: fresh means new, original
men are pieces in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: Students turning out original work.
explanation.definitionFit: Freshmen are first-year students at a college or university.

clue.text: Composer of operas arranged trial with cast

indicators.note: arranged signals that the letters of trial and cast are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An opera composer's work staged as a trial with its cast.
explanation.walkthrough: Alessandro Scarlatti wrote many operas; his son Domenico is known for keyboard sonatas.
explanation.definitionFit: Alessandro Scarlatti was a prolific Italian Baroque writer of operas.

clue.text: Mimic, it appears, provided drink

parts.note: an aper is one who apes, a mimic
if means provided that

explanation.surface: An impressionist turns up, it seems, as long as there is a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal.

clue.text: Withdraw separately? It shows a lack of respect

definitions.text: It shows a lack of respect

parts.note: taken as with, Latin and Italian con
taken as draw, which is to tempt or attract

explanation.surface: Pulling out on one's own seems disrespectful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'separately' tells you to split Withdraw into with and draw, each turned into its own synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt is scorn or disdain, a want of regard for someone.

clue.text: Skips the condiment

explanation.surface: Leaping over the seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to leap or skip playfully; pickled flower buds of a Mediterranean shrub are a seasoning.

clue.text: Part of London Cockney speaker associates with Bow

indicators.note: a Cockney drops initial aitches, so says the word as if without its H

parts.note: an arrow goes with a bow in archery

explanation.surface: A Cockney linked with Bow, the East London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is an East End district, Cockney heartland; Harrow is a northwest London borough. A Cockney says it 'arrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrow is a borough in northwest London, home to a famous school.

clue.text: Part of our capital we get society to look after

parts.note: taken as written
to tend is to look after

explanation.surface: Part of London where we go to keep company in high society.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital meant is London; its West End is the theatre and shopping district.
explanation.definitionFit: London's West End is its theatre and shopping district.

clue.text: Political leader, in short, certain to use force

parts.note: Pres is the abbreviation for President
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A head of state, briefly, confident of using strong-arm tactics.
explanation.definitionFit: To pressure someone is to coerce them, applying compulsion.

clue.text: Fish a shallow stretch of water

explanation.surface: Fish swimming in shallows.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoal is a large group of fish, and also a sandbank or shallow place in the sea.

clue.text: Relaxes in informal clothes

explanation.surface: Someone unwinding in casual wear.
explanation.definitionFit: To slack is to ease off; slacks are casual trousers.

clue.text: Confine a black-hearted murderer

indicators.note: hearted signals that the letter for black sits in the middle of the murderer

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Locking up a wicked killer.
explanation.definitionFit: To cabin is an old verb for confining in a small space, as in cabined.

clue.text: Flag of a neighbouring country isn't finished

indicators.note: isn't finished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Irish, of Ireland, the country next to Britain

explanation.surface: A neighbouring nation's banner left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is not a banner but the plant: yellow flag is a wild iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is an old name for the wild yellow plant with sword-shaped leaves.

clue.text: University official cut half the pages — odd

indicators.note: cut means the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: a rector heads some universities, especially in Scotland

explanation.surface: A college head has removed half a book's pages, oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Right-hand pages in a book, which carry odd numbers, are called by this term; the backs are verso.

clue.text: It enables revolutionary movement to upset the board

parts.note: to turn is to upset, as milk turns
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A revolution made possible by overturning the government.
explanation.definitionFit: A turntable is a rotating platform, as for records or locomotives.

clue.text: A cocktail with it? On the contrary

explanation.surface: Asking whether a cocktail is trendy, and being told it is not.
explanation.definitionFit: A whisky-and-bitters drink bears this name; 'with it' means trendy, and its opposite is outdated.
